$Comment: The standalone RpgStations Cooking Fire work station block (scope-2 wave-3 leg W3-F, design section 2.7 fish exemplar, the remote-anchor half of the cutting-board/cooking-fire pair - it is BOTH a standalone direct cook loop AND the multi-station anchor CuttingBoard/PrepFish claims by proximity+type). Model/texture/hitbox lifted from the vanilla Deco_Campfire_Off (ledger [6cdea5ead]) - the diegetic F-loop deliberately keeps its OWN rpg_station_use RootInteraction on Interactions.Use rather than the vanilla Bench_Campfire's auto-open 'Open_Processing_Bench' (the same RPG_Station_Sawmill-vs-Bench_Lumbermill discipline: reuse the model, not the competing Use wiring). THREE states, one per custody phase (Server/RpgStations/Stations/CookingFire.json's Custody.States = {Empty:'Default', Loaded:'Loaded', Working:'Lit'}): Default = the unlit Campfire_Off model/texture with the empty hint; Loaded = the SAME unlit look with the loaded hint (raw fish is sitting on a COLD fire - the Custody.Display prop is the has-fish signal, the block itself must not burn); Lit = the actively-cooking look, held ONLY while a cook/convert step is genuinely running (maintainer ruling 'Lit = actively cooking', engine side StationService#enterWorkingState). The Lit field set is copied VERBATIM off vanilla Furniture_Crude_Brazier.json, the one vanilla block using this exact Campfire.blockymodel + Campfire_Texture.png pair: the animated Fire_Burn blockyanim + Looping, Light #ecb (Bench_Campfire's own Processing-state colour), BlockSoundSetId Campfire, the looping crackle AmbientSoundEventId SFX_Campfire_Default_Loop, and the Campfire_New_Cartoon particle system (flames + Fireplace_Sparks_Up embers + heat distortion) at the brazier's own Scale 0.9 / +0.25Y offset, beside the pre-existing Smoke_Black plume which stays. Crackle + embers are therefore 100% NATIVE and need ZERO engine work: BlockType per-state AmbientSoundEventId is LOOPING-validated ('a looping ambient sound event that emits from this block when placed') and per-state Particles run for the state's whole lifetime, both starting and STOPPING automatically on the setBlockInteractionState flip with no stop packet (none exists in the protocol) - the exact mechanism vanilla Bench_Campfire uses for its own Processing state. VariantRotation is authored NESW (a station-block placement convention, deliberately over the vanilla decorative RandomRotation) so the block's own facing composes correctly with Custody.Display's facing-relative Offset. When claimed as a remote anchor by another station's program, this block's OWN action is never invoked (design 2.2) - only its Custody claim and block state matter there. NATIVE-BENCH ROUTE REMOVED (decision 65, maintainer ruling 2026-07-29): this block used to ALSO carry a native BlockType.Bench{Type:Processing,Id:Campfire} + BlockType.BlockEntity.Components{BenchBlock,ProcessingBenchBlock} (decision 51a), authored for one reason only - so the engine's sneak+F handler could open the vanilla processing WINDOW over the same Food_Fish_Raw -> Food_Fish_Grilled recipe. The maintainer ruled the native crafting menu off the cooking fire, so all three keys are GONE and the engine-side opener (station/StationBenchWindow.java) plus its Route.BENCH branch were deleted with them - sneak+F is picker-or-toggle everywhere now, and since this station derives no output CATEGORIES (its one Conversion is hand-authored and untagged), sneak+F here simply falls through to the plain diegetic toggle. Nothing else depended on the Bench identity: Interactions.Use was always this mod's own rpg_station_use RootInteraction, never the vanilla auto-open, so removing Bench changes no other behavior. Recipe.FromCrafting.Benches:['Campfire'] in the STATION asset (Server/RpgStations/Stations/CookingFire.json) is a different mechanism entirely (recipe DERIVATION, StationRecipeDeriver) and is deliberately untouched.
